canonical_question: Why did the authors attribute grain refinement exclusively to the 'cascade effect' rather than the 'ballistic mixing' or Frenkel-pair production from the 16 keV He ions?

question_variants.question: Why did the authors attribute grain refinement exclusively to the 'cascade effect' rather than the 'ballistic mixing' or Frenkel-pair production from the 16 keV He ions?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The authors attribute grain refinement exclusively to the cascade effect because refinement was only observed when heavy ions were introduced. He-only irradiation produced defects but no refinement, indicating the cascade effect (from heavy ions) is the necessary condition, whereas ballistic mixing or Frenkel-pair production from He alone were insufficient.

answers.answer: The authors attribute grain refinement to the cascade effect because the results demonstrate that refinement only occurred when heavy ions were introduced. The text states: 'The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced. This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.'
answers.measurement_outcome: grain refinement and fragmentation observed only in dual-beam case
answers.mechanism: cascade effect from overlapping cascades larger than grain size
answers.boundary_limitation: He-only case generated defects but no refinement
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time
